docGuides.title: How to get these documents
docGuides.lead: Practical notes for the documents your schemes ask for. Fees and timelines vary by state — treat these as typical, not exact.

aadhaar.name: Aadhaar card
aadhaar.where: Any Aadhaar Seva Kendra or Common Service Centre (CSC); book or locate one on uidai.gov.in.
aadhaar.cost: First enrolment is free; most updates cost about ₹50.
aadhaar.time: Enrolment takes minutes; the card arrives by post within about 30 days. The enrolment slip works as proof sooner.

bank_account.name: Bank account / passbook
bank_account.where: Any bank branch, India Post Payments Bank, or a banking correspondent. Ask for a Jan Dhan (PMJDY) account — zero balance, no charges.
bank_account.time: Usually opened the same day with Aadhaar.

caste_certificate.name: Caste / category certificate
caste_certificate.where: Your tehsil / SDM office, or your state’s e-district portal online.
caste_certificate.cost: Free to about ₹50 depending on the state.

income_certificate.name: Income certificate
income_certificate.where: Tehsil / revenue office, or your state’s e-district portal.
income_certificate.time: Typically 1–3 weeks. Note: most states treat it as valid for 6–12 months, so check yours is current.

bpl_card.name: BPL listing
bpl_card.where: Your gram panchayat or the district food & civil supplies office keeps the BPL / SECC list; ask them to check your family’s inclusion.
bpl_card.time: The check itself is quick; adding a family to the list is a state process that can take much longer.

ration_card.name: Ration card
ration_card.where: Your state food & civil supplies department — online portal or the local ration office.

land_records.name: Land records (khasra / khatauni)
land_records.where: Your patwari or tehsil office; most states also give instant online copies on their bhulekh / land-records portal.
land_records.cost: Online copies are free or a few rupees; certified copies cost a small fee.
land_records.time: Online: immediate. Certified copy: a few days.

disability_certificate.name: Disability certificate / UDID
disability_certificate.where: The medical board at a government hospital; apply for the UDID card on swavlambancard.gov.in.
disability_certificate.time: A few weeks including the medical assessment.

age_proof.name: Proof of age / birth certificate
age_proof.where: The municipal body or gram panchayat where the birth was registered; a school-leaving certificate usually also works.
age_proof.time: Typically 1–2 weeks for a fresh copy.

residence_proof.name: Residence / domicile certificate
residence_proof.where: Tehsil office or your state’s e-district portal.

death_certificate.name: Death certificate
death_certificate.where: The municipal body or gram panchayat where the death was registered.
death_certificate.cost: Free to nominal (first copy is often free).

home.heroTitle: Find out exactly what government support you’re entitled to
home.heroLead: Answer a few plain questions. Adhikaar checks the official rules of {schemeCount} central and Uttar Pradesh government schemes, shows its work — every claim linked to the government’s own words — and helps you prepare each application.
home.heroNote: Free · No login · Takes about 3 minutes
home.howLead: Three steps from your situation to a report you can keep.
home.step1Body: A few plain questions about your age, work, and household. No login, no documents, and nothing is stored.
home.step2Body: Your answers are tested against each scheme’s actual eligibility clauses — by rules written from the government’s own text, not by guesswork.
home.step3Body: For every scheme: why you qualify, each claim linked to its official source — and an application packet with the documents to gather, the official steps, and what to confirm at the office.
home.differentTitle: Most tools search and summarise. Adhikaar decides — and proves it.
home.differentBody1: A chatbot that merely retrieves scheme text can sound confident and still be wrong — and a wrong “you qualify” costs real people real time and hope. Adhikaar works differently: every eligibility rule is written down from the official clause, your answers are checked against those rules deterministically, and a verifier confirms every sentence of the explanation against the source before you see it.
home.differentBody2: When we tested both approaches on the same cases, the plain-language AI invented 16 entitlements that didn’t exist.
home.differentBody2End: And when it doesn’t have enough information, it asks — it never guesses.
home.flowRetrieved: Official rules retrieved from government text
home.flowVerifier: Verifier checks every claim against the source
home.closingTitle: Three minutes. No login. A packet you can take to the office.

about.title: Adhikaar means “right” — because that’s what these are
about.intro1: India runs some of the largest welfare programmes in the world, but knowing what you’re entitled to still takes expertise most people don’t have: the rules live across portals and PDFs, in language written for administrators. Many entitlements go unclaimed not because people don’t qualify, but because they never find out they do.
about.intro2: Adhikaar is an attempt to close that gap carefully. It answers one question — “what am I entitled to?” — for {schemeCount} central and Uttar Pradesh schemes, in plain language, with every claim traceable to the government’s own text, and then helps prepare the application. It would rather say “not sure, ask this at the office” than be confidently wrong.
about.openBody: The whole system is open: the rules files (one clause of official text per rule), the evaluation dataset and results, and this site. If you find a rule that’s wrong or out of date, you can point at the exact line — and fix it.
about.linkSource: Source code and rule files on GitHub
about.privacyBody: There are no accounts and no database of people. Your answers live in your browser — in the link or resume code you choose to keep, or in a case file you choose to save on your device or export. They are sent to the eligibility engine only to compute your report, and are not stored there.
about.contactBody: Found a mistake in a rule, or want to help cover more schemes?
about.contactEnd: — corrections are the most valuable contribution this project can get.

trust.title: Every answer, traced to its source
trust.intro: Adhikaar decides eligibility from the government’s own words, not a summary of them. Every rule is written from an official clause and carries a link to the exact scheme page it came from. This page shows the provenance of the whole rule base — and how we know it’s still current.
trust.statSchemesNote: official pages re-fetched and diffed against our audited copy
trust.statRulesNote: each one links to the exact government source
trust.statDriftNote: official text that changed and is queued for human review
trust.howBody: A monitor re-fetches every myScheme-sourced page, cleans it the same way as our committed copy, and diffs the meaning-bearing sections. Wording changes in eligibility, exclusions, benefits, or documents are flagged for a human to re-audit before any verdict relies on them.
trust.tableCaption: Live schemes the eligibility check decides on. Each links to its official source and rule breakdown.
trust.disclaimer: “Verified” means the official page text matched our audited copy on the last monitor run — not that eligibility was individually re-confirmed. Government text can change at any time; always confirm on the official portal before acting.
trust.ctaTitle: See a full rule-by-rule breakdown for any scheme.

lifeEvents.ctaNote: About 3 minutes · No login · Answers stay on your device
lifeEvents.widowedLead: A monthly widow pension and survivor benefits exist, but many go unclaimed simply because nobody says so at the office. Answer a few plain questions and see exactly what you can claim — every answer backed by the official rules.
lifeEvents.pregnantTitle: Expecting a child? Check what support you can claim now
lifeEvents.pregnantLead: Health cover and family-support schemes have specific windows — some must be claimed during pregnancy or soon after birth. A few questions show what applies to you, with the official text to take along.
lifeEvents.farmerTitle: Farming a small holding? Some support is yours by right
lifeEvents.farmerLead: Income support, crop insurance, and pension schemes exist for farming families — with exclusions that are hard to guess. Check which ones your household can actually claim, cited to the official rules.
lifeEvents.studentTitle: Scholarships your family may be missing
lifeEvents.studentLead: Post-matric scholarships and education support depend on category, income, and course — rules that are easy to misread. Answer for the student in your family and see what applies, with sources.
lifeEvents.seniorTitle: Past 60? A monthly pension may already be yours
lifeEvents.seniorLead: Old-age pensions are small but real, and the eligibility rules are precise. Two minutes of questions show whether you or a parent can claim one — and exactly what to take to the office.
lifeEvents.disabilityTitle: Living with a disability? Check your entitlements
lifeEvents.disabilityLead: Disability pensions and support schemes depend on the certified disability percentage and a few facts about your household. See what the official rules say you can claim.

howItWorks.title: Built so you can check its work
howItWorks.intro: Most AI tools answer eligibility questions by searching documents and summarising what they find. That can sound right and be wrong. Adhikaar separates the jobs: language models only read and explain — a deterministic rules engine decides, and a verifier checks every claim against the official text before you see it.
howItWorks.pipelineTitle: From your answers to a cited report
howItWorks.pipe1Body: You answer a few plain questions — age, work, household. No login, and nothing is stored anywhere.
howItWorks.pipe2Body: The scheme text comes straight from government sources — myScheme and official guidelines — kept with its section labels and source links. {schemeCount} central and Uttar Pradesh schemes, {ruleCount} encoded rules.
howItWorks.pipe3Title: A rules engine decides — not the AI
howItWorks.pipe3Body: Each eligibility clause is written down as an executable rule. Your answers are checked against them deterministically: met, not met, or unknown. Unknown never becomes a guess — it becomes a question.
howItWorks.pipe4Body: Before anything reaches you, every sentence of the explanation is checked against the official text it cites. Claims that can’t be verified are dropped.
howItWorks.pipe5Body: Every verdict comes with the exact clause it rests on, a link to the official source, and honest “likely” wording where the office still has to verify a fact. Each scheme you qualify for gets an application packet built from its official page.
howItWorks.measuredLead: We tested the rules engine against a plain AI baseline on the same 41 labeled cases — same retrieval, same underlying model, only the decider differs.
howItWorks.statFpCaption: false entitlements asserted by the rules engine (the AI baseline asserted 16)
howItWorks.statAccCaption: eligibility accuracy, against 57% for the AI-only baseline
howItWorks.statFaithCaption: more of its claims verifiably supported by the cited official text
howItWorks.measuredNote: Small labeled evaluation set — treat these as engineering counts, not population statistics. The full methodology and raw results are in the open-source repository.
howItWorks.prin1Body: A wrong “you qualify” costs real people bus fare, queues, and hope. The rules engine can only conclude what the encoded official clauses support. In our evaluation it asserted zero false entitlements across 92 judgments — the AI-only baseline asserted 16.
howItWorks.prin2Body: Eligibility rules have three outcomes here: met, not met, and unknown. Anything unknown turns into a question or an honest “needs one more detail” — never a silent assumption.
howItWorks.prin3Title: Some facts only the office can verify
howItWorks.prin3Body: Whether your family is on the BPL or SECC list can’t be checked from a conversation. Verdicts that rest on such facts are marked “likely eligible” and the report says exactly what to confirm.
howItWorks.prin4Body: Every scheme page shows the date its official text was fetched and verified. If the text is a transcription (one scanned PDF is), that’s disclosed too.
howItWorks.prin5Title: Preparing the application, not just the verdict
howItWorks.prin5Body: Each application packet lists the documents from the scheme’s own page — or says honestly that the page lists none — with the official steps as written. Missing documents across all your schemes are ranked by how many schemes each one unlocks.
howItWorks.prin6Title: A person stays in the loop
howItWorks.prin6Body: At a CSC or Jan Seva Kendra, an operator can switch on assisted mode and mark the proofs they have seen. That shows as a note beside the verdict and on the printed hand-off — the verdict itself only ever comes from the rules.
howItWorks.limitCoverage: The eligibility check decides {schemeCount} central and Uttar Pradesh schemes today. {pendingCount} more are documented in the catalog with machine-drafted rules awaiting human verification — each joins the check only when a person has certified every rule against its official source.
howItWorks.limitOutOfScope: One more is listed for reference only: its applicant is an institution, not an individual, so a personal check can’t apply.
howItWorks.limitStates: Of the state schemes — often the most relevant — only Uttar Pradesh’s are covered so far. For every other state, “not eligible here” never means “not eligible anywhere”.
howItWorks.limitSelfReported: Answers are self-reported. The final decision always rests with the implementing authority, and the report is designed to be taken to them — not to replace them. Where a verdict rests on a fact only the office can verify (BPL or SECC lists), the report says exactly what to confirm and where.
howItWorks.limitSimplified: A few rarely-triggered criteria are simplified — for example, notified-crop areas (PMFBY), the two-accounts-per-family cap (Sukanya Samriddhi) and Kanya Sumangala’s twins exception are not encoded. Every simplification is listed in the open-source rule files, beside the rule it affects.
howItWorks.limitLanguages: Beyond English and Hindi, the other nine languages are machine-translated and still awaiting native-speaker review — wording may be imperfect in places.
howItWorks.closing: The best way to understand it is to try it.

about.title: About you
about.lead: Most schemes depend on age and life situation — this is the foundation of your report.

place.title: Where you live
place.lead: A few schemes work differently in villages and cities.

work.title: Your work and income
work.lead: This helps us check farmer, vendor, artisan, and income-linked schemes.

work-details.title: A little more about your work

household.title: Your household
household.lead: These answers decide the housing, health, and cooking-gas schemes.

family.title: You and your family
family.lead: Last set — pensions, insurance, savings, and health cover.

age.label: Your age
age.help: In years. Most schemes have an age window, so this matters a lot.
age.errorText: Please enter your age — most schemes depend on it.

gender.label: Gender
gender.whyWeAsk: Some schemes are only for women — like the widow pension and the daughters' savings scheme. We never store this.

marital_status.label: Marital status
marital_status.whyWeAsk: The Indira Gandhi Widow Pension depends on marital status. We only use this to check that one rule.

state.label: State or union territory
state.help: Central schemes apply across India. If you live in Uttar Pradesh, we also check its state schemes.

area.label: Do you live in a village or a city?
area.help: Housing support, for example, is currently for rural areas.

occupation.label: What best describes your main work?

annual_family_income_inr.label: Your family's yearly income (₹)
annual_family_income_inr.help: Everyone in the household together, before tax. A rough estimate is fine.
annual_family_income_inr.whyWeAsk: Several schemes have an income ceiling — for example ₹2.5 lakh a year for the SC scholarship. Your answer is only compared against those limits and never stored.

pays_income_tax.label: Did anyone in your family pay income tax last year?
pays_income_tax.help: Some schemes exclude income-tax payers. “Not sure” is a fine answer.

is_farmer_with_land.label: Does your family own cultivable land in its own name?
is_farmer_with_land.help: PM-KISAN support goes to landholding farmer families.

cultivates_crops.label: Do you grow crops on that land?
cultivates_crops.help: Crop insurance applies to farmers actually growing notified crops.

has_land_ownership_or_tenure_docs.label: Do you have land papers — ownership or tenancy documents?

holds_constitutional_or_political_post.label: Has anyone in your family held a constitutional post or elected office — minister, MP, MLA, mayor, or district panchayat chairperson?
holds_constitutional_or_political_post.help: PM-KISAN excludes families of such office-holders.

is_practicing_registered_professional.label: Is anyone in your family a practicing registered professional — doctor, engineer, lawyer, chartered accountant, or architect?
is_practicing_registered_professional.help: PM-KISAN excludes families of practicing registered professionals.

has_vending_certificate_or_lor.label: Do you have a vending certificate or a letter of recommendation from your town body?
has_vending_certificate_or_lor.help: PM SVANidhi loans ask for one of these. If not, your town's vending committee can issue it.

is_vishwakarma_trade_artisan.label: Is your craft one of the 18 traditional trades — like carpenter, blacksmith, tailor, potter, cobbler, or goldsmith?
is_vishwakarma_trade_artisan.help: PM Vishwakarma supports these listed family trades.

is_post_matric_student.label: Are you studying after Class 10 (post-matric)?
is_post_matric_student.help: The SC scholarship covers courses after Class 10.

social_category.label: Social category
social_category.whyWeAsk: The Post-Matric Scholarship is specifically for SC students, so we can only check it with this answer. It is never stored or shared.

safai_mitra.label: Safai Mitra (sanitation worker or waste picker)

minority.label: Minority (Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain, Parsi)

has_bpl_card.label: Is your family on the BPL list, or do you hold a BPL / priority ration card?
has_bpl_card.whyWeAsk: Pension and cooking-gas schemes use the BPL list. Since we can't check the list itself, a “yes” makes those verdicts “likely eligible”, to be confirmed at the office.

house_type.label: What kind of house do you live in?
house_type.help: Rural housing support goes to families in kutcha houses.

kutcha.label: Kutcha
kutcha.description: Mud, thatch, or other temporary materials

has_lpg_connection.label: Does your household already have an LPG gas connection?

owns_motorized_vehicle.label: Does anyone in the family own a motorised vehicle — a car, tractor, or two-wheeler?
owns_motorized_vehicle.help: A few schemes use this to identify better-off households.

has_bank_account.label: Do you have a bank account?
has_bank_account.help: Insurance and pension schemes pay through a bank account.

family_member_in_govt_service.label: Is anyone in your family a serving or retired government employee?

receives_govt_pension_over_10k.label: Does anyone in the family receive a government pension of ₹10,000 or more a month?

receives_other_govt_pension.label: Do you already receive a pension under another state or central government scheme — old-age, widow, disability or similar?
receives_other_govt_pension.help: Uttar Pradesh's widow and divyang pensions are not paid alongside another government pension.

daughter_age.label: If you have a daughter under 10, how old is she?
daughter_age.help: The Sukanya Samriddhi savings account can be opened until she turns 10. Skip this if it doesn't apply.

number_of_children.label: How many children are in your family?
number_of_children.help: Uttar Pradesh's Kanya Sumangala Yojana is for families with at most two children. Skip this if it doesn't apply.

is_pregnant.label: Are you currently pregnant?
is_pregnant.help: Maternity benefit schemes need this to check eligibility.

single_girl_child.label: Are you the only girl child in your family (no brother)?
single_girl_child.whyWeAsk: A few scholarships are reserved for a family's single girl child. We only use this to check those, and nothing is stored.

disability_percent.label: If you live with a disability, what percentage is on your certificate?
disability_percent.whyWeAsk: The Indira Gandhi Disability Pension needs 80% or more. We ask for the number only to check that rule, and it is never stored.

disability_type.label: Which category is on the disability certificate?
disability_type.whyWeAsk: Some disability schemes apply only to specific categories named in the National Trust Act. Leave this blank if you're not sure.

options.label: Prefer not to say / not sure

bereavement_event.label: Has the main earner of your family passed away?
bereavement_event.whyWeAsk: The National Family Benefit Scheme gives a one-time payment to a poor family whose primary breadwinner has died. We ask only to check that scheme.

is_pmjay_priority_category.label: Is your family in a deprived or priority group — for example landless labourers, or listed in the SECC survey?
is_pmjay_priority_category.help: Ayushman Bharat health cover uses these categories. “Not sure” is fine — many families are listed without knowing.
